styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Pyramids, the Egyptian Museum and Islamic Cairo.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Mosques, bazaars and the Nile at sunset.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Koshari, grilled meats and street snacks.

stays.why: Central for the Egyptian Museum, metro and cheap eats. Lively and noisy; good value.
Quiet island district with cafés and embassies. Calmer evenings, easy taxis to most sights.
Closest to the Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum. Far from Downtown sights.
Near the airport and quiet streets. Best for early flights or a last night.

food: Try koshari: rice, lentils and pasta with tomato sauce. Cheap and filling, often under EGP 100.
Street snacks: ta'ameya (herb falafel), ful medames and fresh baladi bread. Look for busy stalls.
Grilled meats and pigeon are Cairo classics. Ask for the price before ordering at tourist-area restaurants.
Sweet tooth? Try basbousa and kunafa from a local sweet shop, sold by weight.
Tap water is not for visitors; drink bottled water and be careful with raw salads at cheap places.
more_time: Add a day for Islamic Cairo: the Citadel, Sultan Hassan Mosque and Khan el-Khalili bazaar.
Swap a city day for Saqqara and Dahshur to see older pyramids with fewer crowds.
Take a short Nile dinner cruise or a felucca ride at sunset instead of an evening indoors.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Pyramids, the Egyptian Museum and a full day in Islamic Cairo without rushing in the heat.

month_notes: January: cool days around 19°C and cold nights near 9°C. Bring a jacket.
February: mild and dry, highs near 21°C. Great for walking the old city.
March: warming to 25°C. Pleasant, with a little dust possible.
April: hot afternoons near 30°C. Start sightseeing early.
May: hot at 34°C. Plan indoor sights at midday.
June: very hot, highs near 37°C. Drink plenty of water.
July: peak heat at 38°C. Go out at sunrise or after sunset.
August: hottest and muggiest, highs near 38°C. Keep plans light.
September: still hot at 36°C but slowly easing.
October: comfortable again around 32°C. Good month to visit.
November: mild at 27°C. Excellent for the Pyramids and bazaars.
December: cool days near 22°C and chilly nights. Pack layers.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert climate: sunny most days, almost no rain, and a very hot summer from June to September.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Days around 19–27°C and cool nights. Ideal for the Pyramids and long walks.

items.title: Summer is extreme (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 36–38°C. Do outdoor sights at sunrise; stay indoors at midday.

items.title: Almost no rain
items.text: Only about 1–2 rain days a month in winter. No umbrella needed most of the year.

items.title: Dust and haze
items.text: Spring can bring dusty winds that blur the skyline. Check the air before desert trips.

items.title: Cool evenings in winter
items.text: Nights drop near 9–11°C from December to February. A jacket helps after dark.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a hat and sunscreen; a warm layer for winter nights; modest dress for mosques.

transit.best: Metro for cheap cross-city trips; Uber or Careem for everything else.

modes.text: Three lines, clean and cheap; tickets EGP 8–20 by distance.
Red-white-blue city buses EGP 4–6; air-conditioned EGP 7–12; minibuses EGP 5–15.
White cabs often skip the meter, so agree the fare or pay the fair sum on exit. Uber and Careem work well and are often easier.
Not advised for visitors; traffic is heavy and rules are loose.
Fine in some districts, but crossings and pavements are poor; little cycling.
